security_audit.summary: Nine findings are confirmed: unpinned npx installation commands and belt workflows that invoke external search, browser, code-execution, and image-processing services. The other 30 findings are Markdown syntax, documentation links, placeholder URLs, or comparison text. External processing can disclose research inputs, but no malicious intent, credential theft, destructive command, or prompt injection was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before invoking belt apps, especially python-executor, and document provider trust, retention, and data handling.

content.value_statement: Competitive research often becomes scattered and difficult to compare. This skill organizes evidence into feature, pricing, SWOT, review, and positioning deliverables.
actual_capabilities: Guides seven-layer analysis across product, pricing, positioning, traction, reviews, content, and team.
Uses belt applications to search public sources and capture competitor pages.
Builds feature and pricing comparison matrices with support conditions.
Produces SWOT analyses and positioning map structures.
Mines reviews for praise, complaints, switching reasons, and feature requests.
Provides executive summary and detailed report formats.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and authenticated inference.sh access for automated research.
Results depend on the availability and accuracy of external sources.
Placeholder names, URLs, dates, prices, and metrics must be replaced and verified.
Does not validate legal permissions for scraping or using third-party content.

use_cases.title: Plan product strategy
use_cases.description: Compare direct competitors across product capabilities, pricing, positioning, traction, reviews, content, and team signals.

use_cases.title: Prepare a market landscape
use_cases.description: Create an evidence-based summary, SWOT set, and positioning map for planning or investor discussions.

use_cases.title: Equip sales conversations
use_cases.description: Document verified feature differences, plan restrictions, competitor strengths, and switching triggers for competitive sales guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic teardown
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seven-layer teardown of [competitor] for [market]. Use public sources, cite dates, and separate facts from assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare features and pricing
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [our product] with [competitors] across features and pricing. Note plan restrictions, missing evidence, source dates, and competitor strengths.

prompt_templates.title: Mine customer reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze reviews for [competitor] across [sources]. Group praise, complaints, switching triggers, and requests, then explain product opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Build an executive report
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an executive competitive report for [audience] covering market context, SWOT, positioning axes, evidence quality, strategic implications, and monitoring priorities.

output_examples.input: Compare our project management tool with three direct competitors.
output: Feature matrix covering collaboration, API access, SSO, reports, mobile applications, free tiers, and integrations.
Pricing table documenting billing terms, minimum seats, annual discounts, setup fees, and usage charges.
Summary identifying verified strengths, gaps, and opportunities.

output_examples.input: Analyze recent customer reviews for a competitor.
output: Most praised: fast setup, broad integrations, and responsive support.
Most complained: complex permissions, annual contracts, and limited reporting.
Opportunity: simplify administration and provide flexible monthly plans.

output_examples.input: Create a positioning view for four products.
output_examples.output: A two-axis map using self-serve versus sales-led and specialized versus general, with evidence notes for every placement.

best_practices: Date every source and distinguish verified facts from assumptions.
Limit focus to three to five direct competitors with comparable users and use cases.
Include competitor strengths and explain strategic implications after each section.
anti_patterns: Do not present outdated prices, ratings, or market figures without source dates.
Do not rank competitors using vague axes such as good versus bad.
Do not send confidential plans, customer data, credentials, or private screenshots to external research services.

faq.question: Does this skill collect data automatically?
faq.answer: It provides belt commands for search, extraction, screenshots, Python execution, and image stitching. Automated steps require configured third-party applications.

faq.question: Can I use the framework without belt?
faq.answer: Yes. You can apply the matrices and report formats manually, but automated research and visual generation require belt.

faq.question: Does the skill verify competitor claims?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on external sources, so you must verify important claims, prices, ratings, and dates.

faq.question: How many competitors should I analyze?
faq.answer: Focus on three to five direct competitors. Add adjacent alternatives only when they influence customer decisions.

faq.question: Can it create visual deliverables?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for screenshots, positioning maps, and stitched comparison images through external belt applications.

faq.question: How often should I refresh the teardown?
faq.answer: Refresh it quarterly and after major pricing, product, funding, or positioning changes.
